label: STOPP C4: antiplatelet plus anticoagulant in atrial fibrillation
title: Antiplatelet with an anticoagulant in long-term atrial fibrillation
statement: Antiplatelet agents in combination with vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitors in patients with chronic atrial fibrillation, unless there is concurrent coronary artery stent(s) inserted or angiographically proven high grade (> 50%) coronary artery stenosis (no added benefit from antiplatelet agents).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y
source.credit: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: Adding an antiplatelet medicine to a blood thinner in a person with long-term atrial fibrillation adds bleeding risk without extra benefit, unless they have a coronary stent or a tight coronary artery narrowing. Australian guidance differs: after an acute coronary syndrome, people who need a long-term direct oral anticoagulant for atrial fibrillation generally continue it alone beyond 12 months (Heart Foundation and Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand, 2025).

medicine_groups.name: Antiplatelet medicines
medicine_groups.note: Aspirin counts only as a low dose taken daily as an antiplatelet, for example 100 mg. Aspirin used only for pain does not count. A prescribed fraction of a higher-strength tablet counts when the dose and directions support daily antiplatelet use. Asasantin SR is aspirin with dipyridamole. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. CoPlavix and DuoCover contain clopidogrel with aspirin. DuoPlidogrel, Piax Plus Aspirin and APX-Clopidogrel/Aspirin 75/100 each contain clopidogrel and aspirin.

medicine_groups.name: Warfarin, dabigatran and the factor Xa inhibitors
medicine_groups.note: Warfarin is the vitamin K antagonist. Dabigatran is the direct thrombin inhibitor. Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban and fondaparinux are factor Xa inhibitors. No Australian brand is listed for edoxaban. Fondaparinux is an injection. Heparin and enoxaparin are not in this group. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only to people aged 65 or older. If age is under 65, there is no finding. If age is unknown, request the age before confirming a finding. First check for a Group A antiplatelet and a Group B anticoagulant with supply dates that overlap or fall within 60 days of each other. Without matching supplies there is no finding. For the treatment period being assessed, a coronary stent in place, angiographically proven coronary artery stenosis over 50%, or an explicit negative history of chronic atrial fibrillation gives no finding. Confirm a finding only when chronic atrial fibrillation was present during combined treatment and the history explicitly excludes both coronary exceptions. If either clinical fact is missing or its timing is unclear, report only a possible finding. Name each missing fact as applicable: "Chronic atrial fibrillation" and "Coronary stent or narrowing greater than 50% on angiography during combined treatment". If the diagnosis is already documented but its timing is unclear, say that its presence during combined treatment is uncertain. If aspirin is the only candidate antiplatelet, calculate its daily dose from strength and directions, including any prescribed tablet fraction. Ask the pharmacist to judge a borderline dose. If daily antiplatelet use is unclear and the other checks allow a finding, report only a possible finding and ask what dose is taken each day and why. Exclude documented use for pain alone. Cite both supplies and any supporting atrial fibrillation and coronary evidence. For a confirmed finding, cite all four.

needs_facts.meets: The record documents persistent, long-standing persistent or permanent atrial fibrillation. For this criterion it must have been present during combined treatment. Brief episodes alone do not establish chronic atrial fibrillation.

needs_facts.what: Coronary stent or narrowing greater than 50% on angiography during combined treatment
needs_facts.meets: The history explicitly excludes a coronary stent and angiographically proven stenosis over 50%. A condition, procedure history or angiography result documenting either exception excludes the published C4 finding.

options.words: Neither coronary exception applied during combined treatment
A coronary stent was in place during combined treatment
Angiography showed coronary narrowing greater than 50% during that period

cannot_be_seen: Why each medicine was started, whether the atrial fibrillation is long-term, and any stent or angiogram result not recorded here. Also supplies from a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether the antiplatelet is still needed alongside the anticoagulant.
